evals.prompt: Dry-run a re-sync for a repo with existing CLAUDE.md, Gitea agent-work bindings, custom labels and an explicitly declined clean-cut exemption. Its tracker scaffolding needs updating. It also contains owner-edited orchestration policy in orchestrator-policy.json and runtime files in .agent-runtime/. The owner authorizes only workflow-document scaffolding updates, asks to preserve unrelated existing config, and has not requested successor orchestration setup. Show the proposed scope, preservation decision and completion report. Do not edit files or contact a tracker, model endpoint or orchestration service.
evals.expected_output: A bounded scaffolding re-sync that preserves owner answers and unrelated policy/runtime state without configuring orchestration or reviving a declined exemption.
expectations: The proposed writes are limited to the selected instruction file and workflow docs, with owner bindings, custom labels and local edits preserved.
Existing orchestration policy, runtime files and unrelated configuration remain untouched; the agent does not delete, migrate or rewrite them.
The agent does not configure orchestration, invent successor commands or APIs, probe model endpoints or claim an orchestration service is operational.
The declined exemption remains absent; the agent reports the recorded preservation decision without creating a launch gate or repeating an unchanged eligibility interview.
The report distinguishes proposed scaffolding updates from verified writes and preserves the existing CLAUDE.md selection without creating AGENTS.md.

evals.prompt: Dry-run a label-document re-sync using the bundled triage-labels template. The project has an implementation proposal labelled needs-info and workflow:implement; its reporter already answered the product questions, but the agent has not inspected delivered prerequisite code or prepared the bounded brief. The installed document calls workflow:implement build-ready and needs-info waiting on the reporter. The owner reserves readiness authorization to the human. Explain the corrected meanings and next action, preserving the vocabulary and local authority. Do not edit any files, contact a tracker, relabel the issue or authorize implementation.
evals.expected_output: Clarify independent workflow/state dimensions, allocate factual refinement to the agent and preserve the human readiness gate without treating publication as readiness.
expectations: Treats needs-info plus workflow:implement as an incomplete, non-dispatchable implementation proposal rather than an invalid pairing or readiness grant.
Assigns discoverable prerequisite and brief work to the agent with an owner/next action, rather than asking the reporter for facts available in code.
Separates publication approval from the human readiness decision, and preserves dependencies, claims and other execution gates.
Proposes a documentation re-sync without inventing labels, changing the project's execution gates or mutating the consumer project.

evals.prompt: Dry-run a re-sync of an existing Gitea tracker document. Agent work is fixture/app using login eval; origin is GitHub intake and gitea is the agent-work remote. The document currently offers --remote gitea as a substitute for repo scope and its blocking-edge example sends only an index. Preserve the owner's bindings, custom labels, authority rules and protected headings. Show the corrected conventions and an example making issue42 blocked by issue7, including how success is verified. Do not contact either tracker or change this repository.
evals.expected_output: Explicit repository scope, a complete directed dependency payload, verified write semantics and a non-destructive re-sync proposal.
expectations: Repository-specific tea examples use --repo fixture/app; --remote selects a login source, not a replacement for repository scope.
The dependency URL names issue42 and the JSON body includes index 7, owner fixture and repo app.
The agent requires HTTP success and a follow-up dependency read before claiming the blocking edge exists, rather than relying on exit code 0.
The proposal routes shared CLI mechanics to the gitea skill by name and preserves tracker headings, user bindings, labels and authority rules.
No real tracker writes or unsolicited edits to consumer repositories occur.

evals.prompt: Dry-run setup for a repo with AGENTS.md, existing Gitea agent-work bindings and launch decision ticket #13. The owner confirms there are no real users, non-disposable data, external compatibility obligations or contractual/payment commitments, approves a clean-cut policy, and wants existing completed migrations left alone. #13 may close after planning, before release. Produce the proposed instruction paragraph and ticket acceptance criteria, the write/verification order, and the next action on an identical re-sync. The backlog contains migration tickets, but no cleanup was authorized. Do not contact a real tracker or modify this repository.
evals.expected_output: A paired, owner-approved policy and linked launch gate; release-commit verification and transfer of unchecked criteria; idempotent re-sync and no unsolicited backlog edits.
expectations: The proposed policy permits direct clean-cut changes without historical-data migration or compatibility scaffolding, while preserving fresh installs, future runtime correctness and unrelated user work.
The launch criteria require removing the exemption and documenting actual preservation obligations before real users, non-disposable data or commitments, including qualifying beta use.
The go/no-go checklist verifies the release commit, and unchecked criteria transfer to a named release-execution gate if the planning ticket closes first.
The agent verifies the persisted launch gate before activating the exemption and reads back both artifacts.
Re-sync preserves the confirmed decision, updates the existing pair without duplicates, and never reinstalls a retired exemption automatically.
Completed migrations remain untouched and backlog cleanup is offered separately rather than performed.

evals.prompt: Dry-run setup for a repo described as not in production. It has a private beta with paying testers, creator uploads they expect to keep, and a client integration relying on current URLs. AGENTS.md still contains a no-historical-data clean-cut exemption. The owner says to move quickly and keep that paragraph until the public launch. Explain the setup decision, what requires confirmation, and what may be written. Do not contact a tracker or modify this repository.
evals.expected_output: Treat existing preservation obligations, not the deployment label, as decisive; surface the stale exemption and propose explicit obligations without inventing a migration program.
expectations: The agent does not infer clean-cut eligibility from not-in-production or beta labels and identifies the real preservation obligations.
The agent proposes retiring/replacing the stale exemption now and does not rely on its continued presence to ignore obligations.
The agent asks for confirmation of the replacement and keeps unrelated setup available without falsely declaring this policy resolved.
The agent does not erase user data, start historical investigations or migrations, or reopen completed migration tickets.

evals.prompt: Dry-run setup for a repo with only CLAUDE.md and an existing Gitea binding. The owner says it is pre-launch but has not answered whether any data or integrations need preservation. No launch-governing ticket exists. Show the next question; then assume the owner explicitly confirms no obligations and approves the paired clean-cut policy plus creation of a launch gate. Simulate the tracker write failing. Explain the resulting file changes, status and recovery. Do not contact a real tracker or modify this repository.
evals.expected_output: Ask the preservation question, confirm a concrete gate and instruction-file destination, then leave the exemption inactive when its gate cannot be persisted.
expectations: The agent explicitly asks about users, non-disposable data, integrations and contractual/payment commitments instead of treating pre-launch as an answer.
The agent proposes and obtains approval for a launch-execution gate on the agent work tracker; it does not fabricate a ticket URL or use an intake tracker.
The agent respects the existing CLAUDE.md selection without silently creating a conflicting AGENTS.md policy.
After the failed ticket write, the agent does not activate a standalone exemption or report the pair complete; it names the blocker and preserves existing files.
The agent permits unrelated setup to proceed and requires a verified persisted gate before retrying policy activation.
